newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa commission pardons white killer policeman.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa commission pardons white killer policeman.

text.p: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission granted an amnesty on Tuesday to a white apartheid-era policeman serving a life sentence for 11 murders, a commission spokesman said.
Brian Mitchell became the first ex-policeman to be pardoned by Archbishop Desmond Tutu's commission which said he had made a full confession and that the killings were politically motivated.

Mitchell was sentenced to death for each of 11 murders in a notorious killing in December 1988 that became known as the Trust Feeds Massacre. The sentences were commuted in April 1994, on the eve of South Africa's first all-race parliamentary elections, which were won by Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC).
Mitchell told the commission's amnesty committee he had helped to plan and set up an attack on the home of a local leader of the United Democratic Front, the internal arm of the then exiled ANC.
Commission spokesman John Allen said Mitchell was the first former policeman to be pardoned by Tutu's panel. He said further rulings were expected soon.

The commision was set up last year to reveal as much as possible of a dirty war between white minority governments and black liberation groups. It has powers to grant amnesty and indemnity from prosecution to perpetrators who fully confess their deeds.
